event.tagline: Ideas That Resonate. Futures That Emerge.

about.heading: What is TEDxSurreyUniversity?
about.body: TEDxSurreyUniversity is a community-driven TEDx event licensed by TED, bringing together thinkers, builders, and creators to share ideas worth spreading. Expect a full day of inspiring talks, live performances, and meaningful connections.

echoes.heading: Echoes of What’s Next
echoes.bodyHtml: The future is already whispering — in the innovations we create, the questions we ask, and the choices we make today. Echoes of What’s Next invites us to explore how today’s ideas ripple forward to shape tomorrow’s world. Every idea, conversation, and action plays a part in building the world ahead.

whatIsTedx.heading: What is TEDx?
whatIsTedx.body: In the spirit of discovering and spreading ideas, TED has created a program called TEDx. TEDx is a program of local, self-organized events that bring people together to share a TED-like experience. Our event is called TEDxYourCity, where x = independently organized TED event. At our TEDxYourCity event, TED Talks video and live speakers will combine to spark deep discussion and connection in a small group. The TED Conference provides general guidance for the TEDx program, but individual TEDx events, including ours, are self-organized.

aboutTedx.heading: About TEDx (x = independently organized event)
aboutTedx.body: In the spirit of discovering and spreading ideas, TEDx is a program of local, self-organized events that bring people together to share a TED-like experience. At a TEDx event, TED Talks video and live speakers combine to spark deep discussion and connection. These local, self-organized events are branded TEDx, where x = independently organized TED event. The TED Conference provides general guidance for the TEDx program, but individual TEDx events are self-organized. (Subject to certain rules and regulations.)

aboutTed.heading: About TED
aboutTed.body: TED is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization dedicated to discovering, debating and spreading ideas that spark conversation, deepen understanding and drive meaningful change. Our organization is devoted to curiosity, reason, wonder and the pursuit of knowledge — without an agenda. We welcome people from every discipline and culture who seek a deeper understanding of the world and connection with others, and we invite everyone to engage with ideas and activate them in your community. TED began in 1984 as a conference where Technology, Entertainment and Design converged, but today it spans a multitude of worldwide communities and initiatives exploring everything from science and business to education, arts and global issues. In addition to the TED Talks curated from our annual conferences and published on TED.com, we produce original podcasts, short video series, animated educational lessons (TED-Ed) and TV programs that are translated into more than 100 languages and distributed via partnerships around the world. Each year, thousands of independently run TEDx events bring people together to share ideas and bridge divides in communities on every continent. Through the Audacious Project, TED has helped catalyze more than $3 billion in funding for projects that seek to make the world more beautiful, sustainable and just. In 2020, TED launched Countdown, an initiative to accelerate solutions to the climate crisis and mobilize a movement for a net-zero future, and in 2023 TED launched TED Democracy to spark a new kind of conversation focused on realistic pathways towards a more vibrant and equitable future.

people.name: Dr Chris Macdonald
people.title: How virtual reality can cure your fear of public speaking
people.bio: Dr Chris Macdonald is a scientist and founder based at the University of Cambridge. He has a diverse portfolio of professional experience, including work as a consultant and manager for leading-edge tech companies in North America. Upon returning to the UK, Chris established the Immersive Technology Lab to explore the untapped potential of emerging technologies. He later founded the multi-award-winning tech start-up Cambridge VR, which translates his research into real-world impact by developing best-in-class tools for education and healthcare. Dr Macdonald was recently crowned the winner of the 40 Under 40 Award in the highly competitive Science and Innovation category. He is also the recipient of the Digital Health Award, the Digital Education Award, and the Global EdTech Award.
people.Idea statement: What if you could cure any fear? How can we use emerging technologies to revolutionise training, education, and healthcare? How can we ensure such innovations are accessible to all?

people.name: Emily Gill
people.title: Why Human Skills Matter Now More than Ever
people.bio: Emily Gill is the Co-Founder of LEVRA, an award-winning EdTech company solving Human Skills gaps for businesses by using psychometrics, and AI to measure and develop Human Skills, such as communication, teamwork and EQ. A former Finance Lawyer at Clifford Chance, she completed her MBA at the University of Oxford and has been recognised as one of the Top 50 UK Women in Tech. Emily is a Certified Coach (CPCC) and serves as Chair of School Governors at Harris Clapham, championing inclusive education and opportunities for young people. At LEVRA, she is focused on helping organisations build future-ready workforces and ensuring Gen Z in particular have the Human Skills needed to thrive in an AI-driven world.
people.Idea statement: As AI, tech and automation replace low-value tasks, where we as humans will stand out is in our ability to understand, empathise and communicate. Yet we still aren’t teaching these skills in schools, colleges or universities and we continue to label them 'soft skills', when they are anything but 'soft'. Human Skills are the skills of the future, the ones we should be teaching the next generation, and the ones that will shape humankind in the years to come.

people.name: Dr Noelia Noel
people.title: Preserving the Night Sky: Rethinking Satellites for a Sustainable Future
people.bio: Dr Noelia Noël is an astrophysicist and director of employability within Physics at the University of Surrey. With over 120 publications, Noelia’s work bridges astrophysics, environmental science, and social justice. She leads the UK’s first in-orbit test of ultra-black satellite coatings to reduce light pollution. Her leadership has been recognised through the Santander Women 50 Leadership Programme, the Royal Society Pairing Scheme, the 2023 Vice Chancellor Award, and the Employee Network Award 2025. A passionate communicator, she has delivered invited talks at international conferences, science festivals, and Parliament, inspiring audiences to see science as a force for connection and sustainability.
people.Idea statement: Satellites connect us across the globe and help us monitor our changing planet, but their growing numbers are flooding the night sky with artificial light. This scattered glow is erasing the stars and distorting the faint cosmic signals that help us understand our Universe. My talk explores how rethinking satellite design can help us protect one of humanity’s oldest shared treasures — the dark night sky — while building a more sustainable future in space.

people.name: Dr Sarita Sharma
people.title: Skin Ageing Is Inevitable But Decline Is Optional
people.bio: Dr Sarita Sharma is a multi–award-winning skin expert, dentist (qualifying from King’s College London in 1998) and founder of Essex Sanctuary, recognised as the most trusted skin clinic in Essex. With over 21 years of experience in medical aesthetics, her work centres on science-led, reparative and regenerative approaches that help people age well with confidence and self-care. She transitioned into aesthetics, blending clinical precision with a deep understanding of psychology and patient wellbeing. She holds Platinum status with Save Face and is one of the UK’s first recognised experts in ZO Skin Health. Dr Sarita Sharma is the author of the #1 bestselling book “Transform Your Skin to Transform Your Life” and is widely published in professional media.
people.Idea statement: Ageing changes our skin, but it doesn’t have to diminish our confidence. Skin ageing is not something to resist, but a biological process we can influence through science, mindset, and care. When we shift from “anti-ageing” to “pro-ageing well,” we redefine what it means to grow older with confidence, vitality, and dignity.

people.name: Dr Georgia Bowers
people.title: How Theatre Heals the Shame Behind Ageism
people.bio: Dr Georgia Bowers is a Creative Ageing specialist, theatre practitioner, and academic who uses theatre to lobby and advocate for the rights of older adults. Her research explores how participatory theatre challenges ageism, heals the shame it creates, and supports older adults in regaining visibility, confidence, and voice, reshaping how society views ageing. She has collaborated with the Royal Opera House, Chichester Festival Theatre, and London Bubble Theatre, with her work showcased at the British Film Institute, Tate Modern, and featured by the BBC. Georgia leads the BA (Hons) Applied and Contemporary Theatre at Guildford School of Acting, University of Surrey, and her first book, Ageing Onstage: Theatre and Creative Ageing, will be published by Routledge in 2026.
people.Idea statement: Dr Georgia Bowers explores how theatre can confront ageism and form resilience towards ageist-induced shame. In a culture obsessed with youth, older adults are often silenced or pushed to the margins. Through creative collaboration, they reclaim their voices, visibility, and joy, turning theatre into a radical act of resistance and a celebration of ageing fully, courageously, and unapologetically.
